precepts.text: Jeremiah was not taken into Babylon but saw the affliction of our people. Brought into darkness and not into light, compassed with gall and travail, set in dark places: that is the hell, the captivity, his people were catching.
precepts.point: We were trodden down like the mire of the streets, and we are still being stomped on this very day.

note.label: You Are Hated And In Hell

precepts.text: Examine yourselves, whether ye be in the faith; prove your own selves. Know ye not your own selves, how that Jesus Christ is in you, except ye be reprobates? That examine yourselves is the same thing Jeremiah said. Let us search and try our ways.
precepts.point: Thou hast made us as the offscouring and refuse in the midst of the people.

note.label: Prison House of Shadows

precepts.why:
Jeremiah says, “Let us search and try our ways, and turn again to the Lord.” Paul is talking about the same thing: “Examine yourselves, whether ye be in the faith; prove your own selves.” That examine yourselves is the same thing Jeremiah said: let us search and try our ways.

This is a lot of times what we as a people do not want to do: examine ourselves. What is wrong with me? What is wrong with you? Who raised you? Why do you act that way? Why do you do the things that you do?

“Know ye not your own selves, how that Jesus Christ is in you, except ye be reprobates?” You have to prove your own self, whether Christ is in you or not. And that is where turning again to the Lord starts. Jeremiah goes on, “We have transgressed and have rebelled: thou hast not pardoned”, and that is why we are in this state, the condition we are in now. A people who will not examine themselves will never see why the Lord has covered himself with a cloud, and will never turn again to him.

precepts.text: And that, knowing the time, that now it is high time to awake out of sleep: for now is our salvation nearer than when we believed. Salvation is near. It is high time that we wake up from our sleep. In order to wake up, we must start by examining ourselves.
precepts.point: Thou hast made us as the offscouring and refuse in the midst of the people.

note.label: Prison House of Shadows

precepts.why:
Paul says: “And that, knowing the time, that now it is high time to awake out of sleep: for now is our salvation nearer than when we believed.” Salvation is near. It is high time that we wake up from our sleep.

In order to wake up, we must start by examining ourselves, which is what Jeremiah calls for: “Let us search and try our ways, and turn again to the Lord.” What is wrong with me? What is wrong with you? Who raised you? Why do you act that way? Why do you do the things that you do?

Waking up is not only knowing who we are. It is searching our own ways, seeing that “We have transgressed and have rebelled”, and turning again to the Lord, lifting up our heart with our hands unto God in the heavens. The time is short and salvation is nearer than when we first believed, so there is no time left to stay asleep in the condition we are in.

precepts.text: What shall we say then? Is the law sin? God forbid. Nay, I had not known sin, but by the law: for I had not known lust, except the law had said, Thou shalt not covet. I would not know what sin is but by the law. I would not know what lust is. By studying the word of God you are able to self-examine. You are able to search and try your ways.
precepts.point: Thou hast made us as the offscouring and refuse in the midst of the people.

note.label: Prison House of Shadows

precepts.why:
How do we search and try our ways? Paul shows it: “What shall we say then? Is the law sin? God forbid. Nay, I had not known sin, but by the law: for I had not known lust, except the law had said, Thou shalt not covet.” I would not know what sin is, but by the law. I would not know what lust is, except the law told me.

So by studying the word of God, you are able to self-examine. You are able to search and try your ways, by studying and reading the word of God. That is what Paul said, and it is what Jeremiah said: “Let us search and try our ways, and turn again to the Lord.”

Without the law a man has no measure to try himself by; he thinks what he is doing is fine. With the law in front of him, he can see where “We have transgressed and have rebelled”, and why the Lord has not pardoned. The law is the mirror, and the one who reads it is the one who can turn again.

precepts.text: They have cut off my life in the dungeon, and cast a stone upon me: meaning he would never get out. It's talking about Israel in captivity, which goes with political prisoners who have been in there a long time.
precepts.point: Yet did not the chief butler remember Joseph, but forgat him.

note.label: Joseph in Egypt: Then & Now

precepts.why:
After interpreting the butler's dream, Joseph asked him, “think on me when it shall be well with thee,” and “make mention of me unto Pharaoh, and bring me out of this house:” “For indeed I was stolen away out of the land of the Hebrews: and here also have I done nothing that they should put me into the dungeon.” He wanted out of that dungeon.

Notice the prison is called a dungeon. Lamentations uses the same word: “They have cut off my life in the dungeon, and cast a stone upon me.” To cast a stone upon him means he would never get out. It is speaking of Israel in captivity.

That goes with our political prisoners, who have been in there for a long time, cut off in the dungeon with a stone cast over them. Joseph, stolen away and imprisoned though he had done nothing, is a picture of his people in captivity.

precepts.text: They have cut off my life in the dungeon, and cast a stone upon me; waters flowed over mine head; then I said, I am cut off. That is our forefather Jeremiah in the pit. We all have to go through that; write that precept down.
precepts.point: The prophet which prophesieth of peace, when the word of the prophet shall come to pass, then shall the prophet be known that the Lord hath truly sent him. You will be manifest when the mission is accomplished. We have been warning this country over and over, warning our brothers of what is coming; those who take heed will show that this prophet was among us doing his job. That is what you are beginning to see now. That is why we are here, continuing the mission, continually hardening our faces against the wicked.

note.label: Making Our Face Harder Than Their Face

precepts.why:
“The prophets that have been before me and before thee of old prophesied both against many countries, and against great kingdoms, of war, and of evil, and of pestilence.” That is what you see our leadership doing today: prophesying against many kingdoms, of war, of evil and of pestilence.

And what happened to the prophets of old who did that? “They have cut off my life in the dungeon, and cast a stone upon me. Waters flowed over mine head; then I said, I am cut off.” That is our forefather Jeremiah in the dungeon, in the pit, the dungeon where there was no water but mire and he sunk in it, for warning the king. We all have to go through that. Write that precept down.

So we do not stop. We are on the quest, in Ecuador, in Haiti, in Puerto Rico, going to different countries, because this gospel cannot be stopped; the mission must continue. “The prophet which prophesieth of peace, when the word of the prophet shall come to pass, then shall the prophet be known, that the Lord hath truly sent him.” We have been warning this country and our brothers over and over of what is coming. Those who take heed will show that this prophet was among us doing his job, and that is what you are beginning to see now. So we continue the mission, continually hardening our faces against the wicked, even if it leads to the dungeon.

precepts.text: My soul hath them still in remembrance and is humbled in me; this I recall to mind, therefore have I hope. It is of the Lord's mercies that we are not consumed, because his compassions fail not; they are new every morning. The Lord is my portion. We ask forgiveness in the Lord's prayer and he gives it, and we keep playing with sin.
precepts.point: There hath no temptation taken you but such as is common to man; God will not suffer you to be tempted above that ye are able, but will with the temptation make a way to escape. If you understand the joy of the elect you embrace the temptation, because he has your back. He wants you to make it, though there are those appointed to die. Nobody wanted to pay a landlord who tripled the rent in Brooklyn after counting heads across the street; that trial forced us to pool the real estate, carpentry, plumbing, and electrical talent the Lord had among us, and then he blessed us with the building in New York despite the detractors. We never took our eyes off the prize. Do not let anyone take your crown.

note.label: The Divine Orchestration and Purpose of the People You Encounter

precepts.why:
Paul says the things that happened to our fathers “are written for our admonition”. Jeremiah shows how we hold on to them: “My soul hath them still in remembrance, and is humbled in me.” The them is the afflictions and punishments we are supposed to remember for breaking God's commandments in the past, and we are humbled because of it.

“This I recall to my mind, therefore have I hope. It is of the Lord’s mercies that we are not consumed, because his compassions fail not.” Do you hear that? That is the love the Lord has for us, his mercy enduring for ever. He loves you, sisters; he loves you, brothers. His compassions and his mercies fail not.

“They are new every morning: great is thy faithfulness.” His mercies are renewed every day, forgiving us. We say the Lord's prayer, we ask the Lord for mercy and to forgive our transgressions, and he does it. And we are still playing with sin.

“The Lord is my portion, saith my soul; therefore will I hope in him.” So now we are in the posture where he has given us a way to escape the evil all around us.

precepts.text: It is of the Lord's mercies that we are not consumed.
precepts.point: Our soul is escaped as a bird out of the snare of the fowlers. Our help is in the name of the Lord.

note.label: Donald Trump: the Sword of God

precepts.why:
King David says, “If it had not been the Lord who was on our side, now may Israel say”: the Lord was on Israel’s side, “when men rose up against us”, when the nations rose up against us. Think about that. The only reason we are still breathing is the mercy of the Lord.

Lamentations says it plainly: “It is of the Lord’s mercies that we are not consumed, because his compassions fail not.” That we, brothers and sisters, are still here is only because of the Lord. With the weapons Esau has and the weapons the nations have, if the Lord put the spirit on them to do what they do and gave them free reign with us, we would all have been wiped out.

Read on: “They are new every morning: great is thy faithfulness.” “The Lord is my portion, saith my soul”. His compassion does not fail, and that is why Psalms 124 can say the nations did not swallow us up.

precepts.text: It is of the Most High's mercies that we are not consumed, His compassions fail not and are new every morning.
precepts.point: We praise the Most High among the nations now by wearing the fringes and beautiful garments, pushing the gospel in the streets to our people, waking up the dead state of our people while Bishop destroys Christianity week after week.

note.label: Psalm 57: My Heart Is Fixed

precepts.why:
“For thy mercy is great unto the heavens, and thy truth unto the clouds.” “It is of the Lord’s mercies that we are not consumed, because his compassions fail not. They are new every morning: great is thy faithfulness.” It is of the Most High's mercies that we are not consumed; his compassions fail not and are new every morning.

That is why David says “I myself will awake early” to praise him. His mercy is great unto the heavens and new every morning, so the fixed heart sings and gives praise among the people and among the nations.

precepts.text: All our enemies have opened their mouths against us, and these enemies are the nations.
precepts.point: They compassed me about also with words of hatred and fought against me without a cause. For my love they are my adversaries, but I give myself unto prayer. We have to give ourselves unto prayer and let God fight our battles, for it is not by our might.

note.label: Psalm 109: Give Myself unto Prayer

precepts.why:
“For the mouth of the wicked and the mouth of the deceitful are opened against me: they have spoken against me with a lying tongue.” Jeremiah says the same in the captivity: “All our enemies have opened their mouths against us.”

The people speaking against us with a lying tongue are the nations. They are the enemies whose mouths are opened against us, compassing us about with words of hatred and fighting against us without a cause.

precepts.text: It is of the Lord's mercies that we are not consumed, because His compassions fail not; they are new every morning, great is Thy faithfulness.
precepts.point: Gracious is the Lord, and righteous; yea, our God is merciful. Our God is merciful, and this is why we are not consumed.

note.label: Psalm 116: I Love the Lord Because He Hath Heard My Voice

precepts.why:
“Gracious is the Lord, and righteous; yea, our God is merciful.” Because he is merciful, we are still here: “It is of the Lord’s mercies that we are not consumed, because his compassions fail not. They are new every morning: great is thy faithfulness.”

Our God is merciful, and this is why we are not consumed. When the sorrows of death compassed us and the pains of hell got hold on us, we called upon the name of the Lord, and his compassions did not fail; they are new every morning.

precepts.text: The Most High will put all these curses upon our enemies and on them that hate and persecute us.
precepts.point: Jeremiah prayed for the Most High's curse on the enemy because he knew the heathen would have to go through the curses of Deuteronomy 28 when it is all said and done; we are the ones redeemed from the curse, and we will see our enemies go through it for eternity while we reign forever.

note.label: Lamentations 3: Affliction, and Hope in the Most High's Mercies

precepts.why:
Jeremiah prays, “Render unto them a recompence, O Lord, according to the work of their hands. Give them sorrow of heart, thy curse unto them.” He prayed for the Most High's curse on the enemy because he knew what was written: “And the Lord thy God will put all these curses upon thine enemies, and on them that hate thee, which persecuted thee.”

The heathen will have to go through the curses of Deuteronomy 28 when it is all said and done. The Most High will put all these curses upon our enemies and on them that hate and persecute us; that is the recompence according to the work of their hands, and Jeremiah asked for it out of the low dungeon.

precepts.text: Christ redeemed us from the curse of the law, so Israel alone is delivered from the curses of Deuteronomy while the other nations must go through them.
precepts.point: Jeremiah prayed for the Most High's curse on the enemy because he knew the heathen would have to go through the curses of Deuteronomy 28 when it is all said and done; we are the ones redeemed from the curse, and we will see our enemies go through it for eternity while we reign forever.

note.label: Lamentations 3: Affliction, and Hope in the Most High's Mercies

precepts.why:
“Christ hath redeemed us from the curse of the law, being made a curse for us: for it is written, Cursed is every one that hangeth on a tree.”

We are the ones redeemed from the curse; Israel alone is delivered from the curses of Deuteronomy, while the other nations must go through them. That is why Jeremiah could pray, “Give them sorrow of heart, thy curse unto them. Persecute and destroy them in anger from under the heavens of the Lord.” The Most High pleaded the causes of his soul and redeemed his life, and we will see our enemies go through the curse for eternity while we reign forever.

precepts.text: It is of the Most High's mercies that we are not consumed, because His compassions fail not, and that is the compassion we are reading about here.
precepts.point: When He is pacified, she shall remember her ways, be ashamed, and never open her mouth anymore because of her shame, and she shall know that He is the Lord.

note.label: Ezekiel 16: The Harlot Redeemed by an Everlasting Covenant

precepts.why:
After everything she has done, the Most High still says, “Nevertheless I will remember my covenant with thee in the days of thy youth, and I will establish unto thee an everlasting covenant.” Why is she not simply wiped out? “It is of the Lord’s mercies that we are not consumed, because his compassions fail not.”

That is the compassion we are reading about here. His compassions fail not, so the harlot is redeemed. He establishes His covenant with her, she shall know that He is the Lord, and He is pacified toward her for all that she has done.

This everlasting covenant, the new covenant of Hebrews 10 and Jeremiah 31, is made only with His people. The notion that our oppressors, who glorified our fall, get the same reward is absolute foolishness and makes no biblical sense. The mercy is toward the one He has a covenant with from the days of her youth.

note.label: The Power Of Hope

precepts.why:
“But let us, who are of the day, be sober”: be sober, be alert, “putting on the breastplate of faith and love; and for an helmet, the hope of salvation.” We must put the helmet on for the hope of our salvation; that is why we are covered by the law, the statutes and the commandments.

“For God hath not appointed us to wrath, but to obtain salvation by our Lord Jesus Christ”. Our salvation is going to come from Christ himself, so what are you worried about? Be patient and endure; your time will come, for the oppression, the affliction, the rape and murder they have done to us.

All these precepts mean nothing if you do not take control of your own mind. Your mind makes it real: everything around us was once a thought. If you are not controlling your mind, somebody else is controlling it. That is why we have to wait upon the Lord.

note.label: The Power Of Hope

precepts.why: “For my hope is in the Everlasting, that he will save you”. Our hope is supposed to be in the Everlasting. “And joy is come unto me from the Holy One, because of the mercy which shall soon come unto you from the Everlasting our Saviour.”

note.label: The God Of Israel Is The God Of Mercy

precepts.why:
“It is of the Lord’s mercies that we are not consumed, because his compassions fail not.” It is of the Lord’s mercies that we are not dead, Israel. We celebrate Tabernacles tomorrow, the Lord’s will, and people make it because of his mercies. “They are new every morning: great is thy faithfulness.” “The Lord is good unto them that wait for him, to the soul that seeketh him.”

“For the Lord will not cast off for ever: But though he cause grief, yet will he have compassion according to the multitude of his mercies.” The Lord is a merciful God, and we forget how merciful God is. But that is not for us to take advantage of or take for granted. It is to build your spirit up and let you know that if you do slip, the Most High is merciful enough to pick you up and forgive you. You shouldn’t want to slip, you shouldn’t be willing to, but if you do, he is there to forgive you.

note.label: SABBATH NOON CLASS: History Repeats Itself - Message From Jeremiah

precepts.why:
Brothers, you have to realize we are God’s chosen people, and that is why we are being punished. When God says “I myself will fight against you”, it is not that he has thrown us away: “For the Lord will not cast off for ever: But though he cause grief, yet will he have compassion according to the multitude of his mercies.”

Though he causes grief, yet will he have compassion. Right now a lot of our people are grieved; they are in pain. Look at what happened in California: a man hung by a tree, and they ruled it a suicide. A lot of our people are tired of the pain of the oppression, but they must realize they have to return to the Most High God. That is the only option we have: we have to return to this Bible, and we have to keep the Most High God’s commandments.

note.label: Standing Tall When The Smoke Clears

precepts.why: We have to just take it, and learn the lesson God is trying to teach us. “Wherefore doth a living man complain, a man for the punishment of his sins?” God is asking why y’all complain so much. The reason all hell is breaking loose is that you are getting punished for your own sin. God is looking at you like you’re crazy.

note.label: Standing Tall When The Smoke Clears

precepts.why:
That sister waited twelve years to be healed. Some of us are very impatient in this truth: we call for counsel on a Thursday and call again the same Thursday. You have to apply the understanding for a period of time before you double back.

“The Lord is good unto them that wait for him, to the soul that seeketh him.” You are not alone. Sometimes we think our prayers aren’t being heard. That’s not the case.

note.label: Lamentations And The Fall Of Teman

precepts.why: Before getting to Lamentations: “For thus saith the Lord God, the Holy One of Israel; In returning and rest shall ye be saved; in quietness and in confidence shall be your strength”. In quietness and confidence shall be our strength. So throughout all the slavery, God says in quietness and confidence shall be our strength. Slavery is not our doom; we return, we rest, and we quietly wait for the salvation of the Lord.

note.label: Lamentations And The Fall Of Teman

precepts.why: For you young men out there, even the one with the shades on: “My son, gather instruction from thy youth up”. You young men, gather instruction from your youth up. Don’t wait till you’re 45 and 50 to say, oh, now I’m going to get my life together. Don’t do that. “So shalt thou find wisdom till thine old age.” That is bearing the yoke in your youth.

note.label: Lamentations And The Fall Of Teman

precepts.why: “If thou hast gathered nothing in thy youth”: brothers, you young men, if you have wasted your life, sat around playing video games, sleeping till 12 noon, you are preparing your lifestyle to be that of a bum. “How canst thou find any thing in thine age?” How are you going to learn anything when you get older? Your mind is stronger when it’s young. Don’t wait till old age: now I want to get a good wife, brother, now I want to get a house. Bro, you almost 60 years old, the hell is this? You ain’t going to do nothing.

note.label: Lamentations And The Fall Of Teman

precepts.why: This is the yoke of Lamentations 3:27. “Take my yoke upon you, and learn of me”: Christ said take my yoke upon you. We all take that yoke now, but it is best to take it when you’re young, before the clock starts ticking. “For I am meek and lowly in heart: and ye shall find rest unto your souls. For my yoke is easy, and my burden is light.” Christ said his yoke is easy, his burden is light.

note.label: Lamentations And The Fall Of Teman

precepts.why: “Wherefore I abhor myself, and repent in dust and ashes.” So when we go back to Lamentations 3:29, he putteth his mouth in the dust because, just like Job, just as we are, we catch hell at times. We bear that yoke, and we go through hard times.

note.label: Lamentations And The Fall Of Teman

precepts.why: Christ in Lamentations 3:30: “I gave my back to the smiters, and my cheeks to them that plucked off the hair”. He gave his cheek to him that smote him. Some people ask how we know Christ had a beard; this is the verse you go to to prove Christ had a beard. So just as Christ was filled full with reproach, so was Jeremiah, so are we.

note.label: Lamentations And The Fall Of Teman

precepts.why: Paul had to address that dumb thought, that God got rid of the Israelites. “I say then, Hath God cast away his people? God forbid.” The answer is no. “For I also am an Israelite, of the seed of Abraham, of the tribe of Benjamin. God hath not cast away his people which he foreknew.” Foreknew means from the past, from the time of Genesis. He has not cast us away. We are down in the dust right now, in a low state, but there is a rising up again.

note.label: Lamentations And The Fall Of Teman

precepts.why: For you doubters out there: “Thus saith the Lord, which giveth the sun for a light by day, and the ordinances of the moon and of the stars for a light by night, which divideth the sea when the waves thereof roar; The Lord of hosts is his name”. Then “If those ordinances depart from before me, saith the Lord, then the seed of Israel also shall cease from being a nation before me for ever.” If the ordinances of the sun, the moon and the stars depart, then Israel ceases; they have not, so the Lord has not cast us off forever. That’s why when you get up you got to look up and see that sun, moon and stars and say thank you Jesus, thank you Lord.

note.label: Lamentations And The Fall Of Teman

precepts.why: Yet will he have compassion according to the multitude of his mercies: “He will turn again, he will have compassion upon us; he will subdue our iniquities; and thou wilt cast all their sins into the depths of the sea.” So remember that stuff you used to do, smoking weed, adultery, child molestation: the Lord says he is going to take all that and cast it into the sea. You got to start your lives anew.

note.label: Lamentations And The Fall Of Teman

precepts.why: What does it really mean that he does not afflict us willingly nor grieve the children of men? “Say unto them, As I live, saith the Lord God, I have no pleasure in the death of the wicked”. That wicked there is us, doing wickedly. “But that the wicked turn from his way and live”: the Lord wants the wicked among us to turn and live. “Turn ye, turn ye from your evil ways”. So all you hoes out there, turn from your evil ways; all you homos out there, turn from your evil ways; all you child molesters out there, turn from your evil ways; all you thieves and liars out there, turn from your evil ways. “For why will ye die”: you got an opportunity, why will you die? “O house of Israel”: that’s the proof he is talking to us.

note.label: Lamentations And The Fall Of Teman

precepts.why: We are the prisoners on this earth. What was read earlier in those books, that our status always seems to be slavery, is Bible based: “Is Israel a servant? is he a homeborn slave? why is he spoiled?” Are the Israelites servants? Anytime you open the Bible, the twelve tribes of Israel are in captivity. It’s like, what the hell is going on here with this people? And here we are today, thousands of years later, still in that same captivity.

note.label: Lamentations And The Fall Of Teman

precepts.why: This helps explain how we are crushed, our rights turned aside and subverted in our cause. “Therefore the law is slacked”: because we are in captivity, God’s law is slacked. “And judgment doth never go forth”: true judgment never goes forth. “For the wicked doth compass about the righteous; therefore wrong judgment proceedeth.” As a result wrong judgment proceeds. The wicked there are all the other nations; it started with the Babylonians, and now we are in Babylon the great, the same metaphor.

note.label: Lamentations And The Fall Of Teman

precepts.why:
The next precept. “Therefore is judgment far from us”: we’re the prisoners of the earth; we want judgment but we’re not getting true judgment. “Neither doth justice overtake us”: we want true justice but justice does not overtake us. “We wait for light, but behold obscurity”: we wait for truth but behold confusion. “For brightness, but we walk in darkness.”

“We grope for the wall like the blind, and we grope as if we had no eyes.” Every man and every woman here and watching has eyes, so what does it mean? We are looking for help in all the wrong places. We see injustice but we make believe we don’t see it. You didn’t just see that there was no justice for Tamir Rice? The wall in this case is the church: we’re in the Baptist Church walking along around the walls, I didn’t see what I just saw, pastor give me a good message of motivation, help me. points: Dr. Joy DeGruy says African people and people of African descent are extremely resilient, ‘matter of fact I think we’re a miracle.’ This is all of the Most High. We got to give credit to the Most High; he’s been merciful unto us.
“It is of the Lord’s mercies that we are not consumed”, “because his compassions fail not.” That’s what it is: the Most High has been merciful to blacks and Hispanics.

The Moynihan report, a document written in 1965, says it too, in its most controversial chapter, ‘the tangle of pathology’: ‘that the Negro American has survived at all is extraordinary; a lesser people might have simply died out, as indeed others have.’ The fact that we’ve even survived what the Most High put us through is amazing. It shows how resilient black people are, and it is of the Lord’s mercies.

note.label: Sabbath Morning Class: Messengers Of The Nation

points: “It is good that a man should both hope”. God said it is good that a man hope: that is the power of hope. “And quietly wait for the salvation of the Lord.” Quietly, brothers and sisters, we wait for the salvation of God's people, which is us. It is good that we hope for the salvation of our people. Don't be a fool out here.

note.label: The Power Of Hope

points: The books written by the white man say it plainly: from the time of Egypt down to our own times the status of this race has been slavery, slaves at all times, in all places, under all forms of government, and they ask who will say that slavery is not their doom. That is Deuteronomy 28 and Jeremiah 2. But slavery is not our doom. Slavery is not our doom forever.

“It is of the Lord’s mercies that we are not consumed, because his compassions fail not.” When we ask our people why we were not destroyed in slavery, they give credit to that man on the screen, Martin Luther King Jr., and say if it wasn’t for him we’d be dead as a people. Us being here today and not consumed has nothing to do with Martin Luther King Jr., who integrated us into white society. It is of the Lord’s mercies. We must start to change our speech and give credit where credit is due.

note.label: Lamentations And The Fall Of Teman

points: “They are new every morning”: God’s compassions are new every morning. Martin Luther King ain’t here now; the Lord’s compassion was here way before Martin Luther King. That is not saying he was an evil dead spot or anything like that; it is saying we must give credit to the Creator, give credit to God Almighty. “Great is thy faithfulness.”

note.label: Lamentations And The Fall Of Teman

points: “The Lord is my portion, saith my soul; therefore will I hope in him.” We got to start to admit that the Lord is our portion, and we got to hope in him. The him is the Lord.

note.label: Lamentations And The Fall Of Teman

points: “The Lord is good unto them that wait for him, to the soul that seeketh him. It is good that a man should both hope and quietly wait for the salvation of the Lord.” So we got to wait for the salvation of the Lord.

note.label: Lamentations And The Fall Of Teman

points: “It is good for a man that he bear the yoke in his youth.” This is for the young men. The yoke is Christ’s yoke; we all take that yoke, but it is best to take it when you’re young, at a youthful age, before the clock starts ticking and you start going down before you’re about to die. Once you reach 35 you’re at your midlife; once you go 36 you’re going down. That goes for the ladies too: get mad if you want, it is what it is, it’s Bible.

note.label: Lamentations And The Fall Of Teman

points: Jeremiah wrote the book of Lamentations. To lament is a passionate expression of grief or sorrow; that is what Lamentations means. Reading this book years ago, it was depressing: why is this in the Bible? Jeremiah was going through it, but it reflects our life.

Read from 27 to get the context: “It is good for a man that he bear the yoke in his youth. He sitteth alone and keepeth silence, because he hath borne it upon him.” The it is the yoke. Brothers, never be afraid to be alone. Sometimes being alone is good: alone time is study time, time to recollect, time to get your life together. You don’t always need a woman in your face 24/7.

note.label: Lamentations And The Fall Of Teman

points: “He putteth his mouth in the dust”: why? Because of that yoke you are catching hell. Just like Job, just as we are, we catch hell at times. We bear that yoke, we try to get our lives together, and we are going to go through hard times at one point or another. “If so be there may be hope”: hope to come up out of that low state.

note.label: Lamentations And The Fall Of Teman

points: “He giveth his cheek to him that smiteth him: he is filled full with reproach.” Just like Christ; Christ is in this verse. Just as Christ, so was Jeremiah, so are we.

note.label: Lamentations And The Fall Of Teman

points: “For the Lord will not cast off for ever”: the Lord will not cast his people off forever. Right now the thought is that God has cast us off forever. He will not cast us off forever, irregardless of what people say, irregardless of what the church system has set up and lied about. We are down in the dust right now, in a low state, but there is a rising up again.

note.label: Lamentations And The Fall Of Teman

points: “But though he cause grief, yet will he have compassion according to the multitude of his mercies.” Yet will he have compassion on who? The Israelites.

note.label: Lamentations And The Fall Of Teman

points: “For he doth not afflict willingly nor grieve the children of men.” He does not afflict us willingly nor grieve us.

note.label: Lamentations And The Fall Of Teman

points: “To crush under his feet all the prisoners of the earth”: the Lord doesn’t want to crush us all under his feet on the earth. We are the prisoners on this earth, that’s us. That is what was read earlier in those books, that our status always seems to be slavery, and it is Bible based.

note.label: Lamentations And The Fall Of Teman

points: “To turn aside the right of a man before the face of the most High”: he doesn’t want our right to be turned aside.

note.label: Lamentations And The Fall Of Teman

points: “To subvert a man in his cause, the Lord approveth not.” So now, as prisoners on this earth, we are being crushed, our rights are being turned aside, and we are being subverted in our cause, and the Lord approves not.

note.label: Lamentations And The Fall Of Teman

points: We are “the prisoners of the earth.” The Lord has us crushed under feet in this captivity, and here are examples of it: our men and women sitting in prison for four decades and more, many of them old men and women now, who went in in their twenties and are in their seventies today.

The Guardian put it out plainly: ‘Black power behind bars’, the black radicals still in prison after four decades, Black Panthers, Black Liberation Army members and the MOVE organization out of Philadelphia, where they dropped C4 on the place they lived and burnt the whole block up. When you go down that list it says they are incarcerated for the murder of a police officer. Those are the same police in the seventies who were doing evil against us, shooting us in the street and beating us in the streets. The murder they are talking about is called self-defense.

With MOVE, one of them had a gun and shot a cop while the cops were shooting at the building, and they charged all of them with it, a lot of them who didn’t even know what was going on. Why didn’t they do that over January 6, when those Edomite cops got killed? They do it with black people. That is the injustice they do in the law.

Most people could care less about our people incarcerated, don’t give a damn. But the little rights we got right now are because of these people that are still incarcerated. And the women are in it too: black women who are political prisoners of the police state, one who was railroaded for standing against police brutality, and one sister that brothers broke out of prison and got on a plane to escape to Cuba, where she lives on asylum. They called her armed and dangerous, and they always try to disrespect our people when they change their names; they want to keep that slave name on you.

note.label: Lamentations And The Fall Of Teman

points: “To turn aside the right of a man before the face of the most High.” Our rights as men are being turned aside before the face of the Most High, and he sees all of it.

That sister in Cuba said it: ‘people get used to anything’; the less you think about your oppression, the more your tolerance for it grows, until people think oppression is the normal state of things, and to become free you have to be acutely aware of being a slave. ‘Never let your enemies choose your enemies for you.’ ‘No one is going to give you the education you need to overthrow them.’ That is why the white man will never tell you that we are the Jews, or that Jesus is black. Nobody is going to teach you your true history and your true heroes if they know that knowledge will help set you free. That is a rare woman, a revolutionary-thinking woman; brothers, if y’all going to get married, find a woman like that. These men and women are incarcerated or on the run because they were trying to keep their sons and daughters from dying at the hands of white supremacy.

note.label: Lamentations And The Fall Of Teman

points: “To subvert a man in his cause, the Lord approveth not.” Our cause has been subverted, and the Lord does not approve of it, but he allows it. He allows it because of the oppression and revolt that we speak against him (Isaiah 59). We revolt against him, so he lets our enemies revolt against us.

One of our sons who died under the hands of white supremacy told his mother, by text, the names of the people who would do it if something happened to him, and his mother is still trying to find out what happened. Nobody talks about it but us. That is what Isaiah 59 and Lamentations 3 are talking about. Then the names go on and on: George Floyd, Tamir Rice, and more and more. There are so many that we can’t even call their names off the top of our heads. That is a cause subverted, and there is no true judgment for our people here in captivity.

It is like the movie Queen and Slim: a racist Edomite cop pulls the two of them over looking for a reason to arrest the brother, she is a lawyer and tells him what he is doing is breaking the law, he pulls his gun to shoot her, the brother jumps him, the gun goes off and the cop dies, and now they’re on the run. The brother was defending himself and her. That is what these men in prison were doing.

note.label: Lamentations And The Fall Of Teman

points: “Who is he that saith, and it cometh to pass, when the Lord commandeth it not?” That’s these preachers. They say a thing and say it will come to pass, when the Lord never commanded it.

note.label: Lamentations And The Fall Of Teman

points: “Out of the mouth of the most High proceedeth not evil and good?” Preachers don’t understand that the Bible talks about evil and good. God does evil in this earth and he does good. A Christian will never preach that; they’ll say the devil made me do it. But God controls the devil. God controls Satan and his army and his minions.

note.label: Lamentations And The Fall Of Teman

points: “Wherefore doth a living man complain, a man for the punishment of his sins?” What you complaining about, brother? Sister, what you complaining about? You’re complaining because you’re being punished for your sins. You kept your legs open every day of the week for Tom, Dick and Harry, now you caught an STD and you mad at God: why God do this to me? Close your legs. And now a brother is willing to take you with your STD, and you tell him you can’t marry him because he’s a little overweight? Sit down somewhere, get married and heal.
So many times we complain about our sins. But when you come in the truth and you know you’re being judged for something you did, you have to deal with it. You have to endure it.

note.label: Lamentations And The Fall Of Teman

points: “Let us search and try our ways, and turn again to the Lord.” Let us search and try our ways means what? Examine ourselves. That is self-examination: taking a moral compass on yourself, like taking an aptitude test. Every man and every woman must examine themselves and find the pitfalls in their own life, because we can only find out what you allow us to see, or what God reveals in the body. Then “turn again to the Lord.”

note.label: Lamentations And The Fall Of Teman

points: “Let us lift up our heart with our hands unto God in the heavens.” Stop teaching your kids to pray with their hands closed. That ain’t what the Bible ever says. Lift up your hands when you pray to the Lord; don’t put your hands together and hide them. Stop teaching your kids to lie.

note.label: Lamentations And The Fall Of Teman

points: “Thou hast covered thyself with a cloud, that our prayer should not pass through.” It feels at times when we pray to the Lord that he ain’t listening, because we’re not getting the result that we want when we pray. The Lord is saying, hold on, it ain’t yet the time.

note.label: Lamentations And The Fall Of Teman

points: “Thou hast made us as the offscouring and refuse in the midst of the people.” That’s what Paul said: the offscouring, like dung, the doodoo of the earth. It was true back then and it’s true today.

note.label: Lamentations And The Fall Of Teman

points: “All our enemies have opened their mouths against us.” All our enemies speak against God’s truth. They think they’re speaking against us, but it’s really against God; it’s against what his law says, his words. Watch how the enemies speak against us: they accuse us day and night, they say they are not guilty for what they did to us because we are in the midst of sin, and they search out our iniquities and push sin on us through the entertainment world.

It reaches into everything. Harvard University’s black female president was put out and replaced. In the hearing in Congress they tried to say she was for murdering Jewish students; she spoke very eloquently. They asked her how far freedom of speech goes and she said it depends; they asked her if it was okay to murder Jews and she said of course not. When they couldn’t get her on that, they came up with a plagiarism accusation and took her out of that position. Not just that: they speak against the prophets too, us.

note.label: Lamentations And The Fall Of Teman

points: Not only do they speak against our people; they speak against the prophets too. “Fear and a snare is come upon us, desolation and destruction.” Brothers and sisters, just as it was back then, it’s going to happen again to the prophets in Tribulation.

note.label: Lamentations And The Fall Of Teman

points: “Mine eye runneth down with rivers of water for the destruction of the daughter of my people.” There’s going to come a day when we’re going to cry. “Mine eye trickleth down, and ceaseth not, without any intermission”: with no stopping of the crying for the destruction of the daughter of our people.

note.label: Lamentations And The Fall Of Teman

points: “Till the Lord look down, and behold from heaven.” We must wait until the Lord intervenes.

Go back to verse 44 with it: “Thou hast covered thyself with a cloud, that our prayer should not pass through.” We’re going to be praying to the Lord for help and assistance, and the Lord ain’t going to help us until verse 50, “till the Lord look down, and behold from heaven.” We got to wait on his good kindness for him to intervene. He’s not going to move when we want him to move.

note.label: Lamentations And The Fall Of Teman

points: “They have cut off my life in the dungeon, and cast a stone upon me.” The dungeon is jail, brothers. There may even come a time when they send certain brothers to Guantanamo Bay, never to be heard of again. They call them political prisoners: you don’t get a lawyer there, nobody represents you, there’s no trial. Some of you don’t know what I’m talking about; look it up.

When it says they have cut off my life in the dungeon and cast a stone upon me, it means you ain’t never getting out; you’re going to die in there. That’s what Jeremiah prophesied about what happened during the time of Babylon, and that’s what he’s also prophesying about during these turbulent times.

note.label: Lamentations And The Fall Of Teman

points: “Waters flowed over mine head; then I said, I am cut off. I called upon thy name, O Lord, out of the low dungeon.” Again, that low dungeon is prison, jail, Guantanamo even.

note.label: Lamentations And The Fall Of Teman

points: “Thou drewest near in the day that I called upon thee”: the day that we call upon the Lord, he will draw near. Then hear the Lord’s response: “thou saidst, Fear not.” Those two words, fear not. That’s the same thing Christ said in Revelation chapter 2: don’t fear what you must suffer, be thou faithful unto death. It’s the same thing.

note.label: Lamentations And The Fall Of Teman

points: “Thou hast seen all their vengeance and all their imaginations against me.” The nations imagine mischief against the prophets, just like they did during the time of Jeremiah. David prophesied about it.

note.label: Lamentations And The Fall Of Teman

points: “Thou hast heard their reproach, O Lord, and all their imaginations against me; The lips of those that rose up against me, and their device against me all the day.” Jeremiah is saying the same thing David prophesied about, the same thing we just read in the Psalms.

note.label: Lamentations And The Fall Of Teman

points: “Behold their sitting down, and their rising up; I am their musick.” I am their music, meaning we are their discussion. They may have code words for us, but we are always their discussion.

When they sit down, when they lay down, and when they rise up in the morning, they’re talking about the Israelites, about our people: how can we keep them in sin, and not only that, how can we make a profit off of it, exploit them.

note.label: Lamentations And The Fall Of Teman

points: Listen good to what Jeremiah says in prayer: “Render unto them a recompence, O Lord, according to the work of their hands.” A recompense is a judgment: do to them according to the evil that they have done to us, Lord.

note.label: Lamentations And The Fall Of Teman

points: “Give them sorrow of heart, thy curse unto them.” God cursed them. You’re never going to read this in church.

note.label: Lamentations And The Fall Of Teman

points: “Persecute and destroy them in anger from under the heavens of the Lord.” You’re never going to hear this in church, you’re never going to hear this in Sunday school, but that’s what the Bible says to say. Meanwhile there’s a grimy Christian on TV swagging and surfing on so-called New Year’s Eve. That ain’t Jesus.

note.label: Lamentations And The Fall Of Teman

points: “We have transgressed and have rebelled: thou hast not pardoned.” Confessing our faults is part of making supplication. We have not been pardoned. We are yet this day in our captivity; we haven't been delivered yet. Your friends run around saying I'm delivered, but we haven't been saved yet. We have to endure until the end to be saved.

note.label: THE DECEPTION OF SIN

points: “Thou hast covered with anger, and persecuted us: thou hast slain, thou hast not pitied.” This shows the Lord isn't playing.

note.label: THE DECEPTION OF SIN

points: “Thou hast covered thyself with a cloud, that our prayer should not pass through.” We rebelled and transgressed, the Lord sent us into captivity, and he covered himself with a cloud so our prayers would not pass through. He put that cloud there because he does not hear sinners.

note.label: THE DECEPTION OF SIN

points: “Thou hast made us as the offscouring and refuse in the midst of the people. All our enemies have opened their mouths against us.” All the other nations have opened their mouths against us. “Fear and a snare is come upon us, desolation and destruction.” This is the current state of Israel right now, because of our lack of obedience. God put that cloud there, he has not pardoned, and we have to go through it.

note.label: THE DECEPTION OF SIN

points: “They have cut off my life in the dungeon, and cast a stone upon me.” That is the jails.

note.label: THE DECEPTION OF SIN

points: “I called upon thy name, O Lord, out of the low dungeon. Thou hast heard my voice: hide not thine ear at my breathing, at my cry.” This is why we keep the commandments of God, so he will hear our prayers. But it won't happen until we acknowledge our offense, acknowledge what we have done, and repent.
